q: In an ER diagram, 'Age' computed from 'Date_of_birth' is an example of a
exp: A derived attribute's value can be computed from other stored attributes; it is drawn with a dashed ellipse.

q: A relation with 5 attributes and 7 tuples has
exp: Degree is the number of attributes (columns) and cardinality is the number of tuples (rows).

q: The set operations union, intersection and difference on two relations R and S require that R and S be
options: union-compatible (same number of attributes with compatible domains)
exp: Set operations need union-compatible relations: same degree and corresponding attributes drawn from the same domains.

q: Table T(x) holds the values 1, 2, 2, 3, NULL. How many rows does SELECT * FROM T WHERE x <> 2 return?
exp: Only 1 and 3 satisfy x <> 2. The comparison NULL <> 2 evaluates to UNKNOWN, so the NULL row is excluded: 2 rows.

q: R(A, B, C, D) has the FDs AB → C and B → D, and AB is the only candidate key. The highest normal form satisfied is
exp: B → D is a partial dependency of non-prime D on part of the key AB, violating 2NF; hence R is only in 1NF.

q: Which of the following statements about functional dependencies is correct (by Armstrong's axioms)?
options: If A → B then B → A
If A → B and A → C then A → BC
If A → BC then B → A
If AB → C then A → C
exp: The union rule (derived from Armstrong's axioms) states A → B and A → C imply A → BC. The others are not valid inferences.

q: In log-based recovery, the main purpose of a checkpoint is to
options: reduce the amount of the log that must be scanned and processed during recovery
exp: A checkpoint records a consistent state, so recovery need only examine log records after the last checkpoint (plus active transactions).

q: In timestamp ordering, transaction T with TS(T) = 5 tries to read item X whose write-timestamp W-TS(X) = 8. What happens?
options: T is rolled back because it would read a value written by a younger transaction
T reads X and R-TS(X) becomes 5
T waits until the writer commits
T is allowed and W-TS(X) is reset to 5
exp: The rule is: if TS(T) < W-TS(X), the read is rejected and T is rolled back and restarted with a new timestamp.

q: In an ER diagram, a diamond shape represents a
exp: Rectangles denote entity sets, ellipses attributes and diamonds relationship sets.

q: An alternate key is
options: a foreign key that is also unique
a key that is allowed to be NULL
a candidate key that was not chosen as the primary key
a key stored in a second table
exp: Candidate keys not selected as the primary key are called alternate keys.

q: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental (primitive) operator of relational algebra?
exp: Fundamental operators are select, project, union, set difference, Cartesian product and rename; intersection can be derived as R − (R − S).

q:
Orders(oid, cust, amt): (1,A,100), (2,B,50), (3,A,200), (4,C,70), (5,B,150). What does this return?
SELECT cust, COUNT(*) FROM Orders GROUP BY cust ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, cust ASC LIMIT 1;
exp: Counts: A = 2, B = 2, C = 1. Sorting by count descending then name ascending puts A first, so (A, 2).

q: A relation is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and
options: no non-prime attribute is partially dependent on any candidate key
exp: 2NF removes partial dependencies of non-prime attributes on a proper subset of a candidate key.

q: Which DBMS component is chiefly responsible for ensuring the Isolation property of transactions?
exp: Concurrency control (locking, timestamps) isolates concurrently running transactions; the recovery manager handles atomicity and durability.

q: Which statement about schedules is correct?
options: Every view-serializable schedule is conflict serializable
Every conflict-serializable schedule is view serializable, and a view-serializable schedule that is not conflict serializable must contain blind writes
Blind writes never occur in any schedule
exp: Conflict serializability implies view serializability; the converse fails only in the presence of blind writes (writes without a prior read).

q: A clustering index is defined on
options: a unique key of an unordered file
a non-key attribute on which the file is physically ordered
only the primary key of a hashed file
exp: A clustering index uses a non-key ordering field, so records with the same value are stored together.

q:
Match the NoSQL system with its model.
1. Redis  2. Cassandra  3. Neo4j  4. MongoDB
P. Document  Q. Graph  R. Key-value  S. Wide-column
exp: Redis is key-value, Cassandra wide-column, Neo4j graph and MongoDB document.

q: In data warehousing, ETL stands for
exp: ETL extracts data from source systems, transforms it to a common format and loads it into the warehouse.

q: When a one-to-many relationship between Dept (one) and Emp (many) is converted to relational tables, the usual approach is to
options: add the primary key of Dept as a foreign key in the Emp table
add the primary key of Emp as a foreign key in the Dept table
create a third table with no keys
merge Dept and Emp into one table with a repeating group
exp: The foreign key goes on the 'many' side, so each Emp row stores the Dept it belongs to.

q: Inserting a tuple with NULL in its primary key attribute violates
exp: The entity integrity constraint states that no primary key attribute may be NULL.

q:
P(id, price): (1,10), (2,30), (3,20). What does this return?
SELECT id FROM P WHERE price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM P WHERE price < (SELECT MAX(price) FROM P));
exp: Innermost MAX = 30; next MAX of prices below 30 is 20, which belongs to id 3 (second highest price).

q: R(A, B, C) has the FD A → B. Which decomposition is lossless?
exp: For {AB, AC} the common attribute A is a key of AB (A → B), so the join is lossless. The others share B, C or nothing, with no key.

q: Which pair of locks on the same data item, held by different transactions, are compatible?
exp: Multiple transactions may read together, so shared-shared is the only compatible combination.

q: A B+ tree allows at most 3 keys per node. When a leaf overflows (4 keys) it splits into two leaves of 2 keys each. Keys 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 are inserted in order. How many leaf nodes exist at the end?
exp: Leaves split at 1-4 into [1,2],[3,4]; at 6 [3,4,5,6] splits into [3,4],[5,6]; 7 goes into [5,6,7]. Final leaves: [1,2],[3,4],[5,6,7] = 3.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the ER model?
exp: A tuple is a relational-model term; entities, weak entities, relationships and attributes belong to the ER model.

q: A relation R(A, B, C) has two candidate keys, A and B (each a single attribute). How many superkeys does R have?
exp: Of the 8 subsets of {A,B,C}, only those containing neither A nor B (the empty set and {C}) are not superkeys. 8 − 2 = 6.

q: Given Student(sid, name) and Enrolled(sid, cid), which expression gives the sids of students not enrolled in any course?
exp: Set difference of all student ids minus ids that appear in Enrolled leaves the students with no enrollment.

q: A(x) = {1,2,3}, B(y) = {2,3,4}. How many rows does SELECT x FROM A UNION SELECT y FROM B return?
exp: UNION removes duplicates, leaving the distinct values 1, 2, 3, 4: 4 rows (UNION ALL would give 6).

q: A table has a column Phone storing values like '98765, 91234' in a single cell. This design violates
exp: 1NF requires atomic (indivisible) attribute values; storing several phone numbers in one cell breaks it.

q: A bank transfers Rs 500 from account A to B. The system crashes after A is debited but before B is credited. On restart A's debit is undone. Which ACID property ensures this?
exp: Atomicity makes the transfer all-or-nothing, so the partial debit is rolled back.

q: Which isolation level is the weakest, permitting dirty reads?
exp: READ UNCOMMITTED lets a transaction read data not yet committed by others (dirty reads); the other levels prevent it.

q: K-means is an example of which data mining task?
exp: K-means groups unlabeled data into k clusters by similarity, which is unsupervised clustering.

q: In a company, each employee works in exactly one department but a department has many employees. The relationship Employee to Department is
exp: Many employees map to one department, so from Employee to Department the cardinality is many-to-one.

q: R(A, B, C) satisfies A → B, B → C and C → A. How many candidate keys does it have?
exp: A+, B+ and C+ each equal {A,B,C}, so A, B and C are each candidate keys: 3.

q: If relations R(A, B) and S(C, D) have no attribute in common, then the natural join R ⋈ S is equivalent to
options: the union of R and S
exp: With no common attributes there is nothing to equate, so every pair combines: the Cartesian product.

q: Names in table P: Anil, Sunil, Anita, Nila, Anand. How many rows does SELECT * FROM P WHERE name LIKE '_n%' return?
exp: The pattern needs 'n' as the second character: Anil, Anita and Anand match; Sunil (u), Nila (i) do not. So 3.

q:
Statement I: Every relation with only two attributes is in BCNF.
Statement II: Every relation in 3NF is also in BCNF.
options: Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
exp: With two attributes every non-trivial FD has a key as determinant, so BCNF holds. BCNF is stronger than 3NF, so II is false.

q: By the pseudo-transitivity rule, if X → Y and WY → Z then
exp: From X → Y, augment with W: WX → WY; with WY → Z, transitivity gives WX → Z.

q: The write-ahead logging (WAL) protocol requires that
options: data is written to disk only after the transaction ends
the log is never written to disk
the log record describing an update be written to stable storage before the updated data page is written to disk
commit records are written after checkpoints only
exp: WAL ensures undo/redo information reaches stable storage before the modified page, enabling recovery.

q: In the growing phase of two-phase locking, a transaction
options: may obtain locks but may not release any lock
may release locks but not obtain any
may neither obtain nor release locks
must release all locks at once
exp: 2PL has a growing phase (acquire only) followed by a shrinking phase (release only).
